title: Citi Thinks Aave Could Become the Go-To Lender for Tokenized Assets. Can AAVE Recover From a 77% Drop?
detail:
Citi Thinks Aave Could Become the Go-To Lender for Tokenized Assets. Can AAVE Recover From a 77% Drop?
Sam Daodu
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 10:00 AM MST 6 min read
AAVE-USD
C
SOFI

Quick Read

Citi Research named Aave the go-to lending layer for tokenized collateral, yet AAVE sits 77% below its $662 all-time high.

JPMorgan's Kinexys Tokenized Collateral Network competes directly with Aave for institutional flows, and AAVE plays no role in Horizon's lending operations.

AAVE's recovery requires a named institution to publicly commit tokenized collateral to Horizon and push the token back above its recent $188 high.

It sounds nuts, but SoFi is giving new Active Invest users up to $1,000 in stock for a limited time, and all it takes is a $50 deposit to get started. See for yourself (Sponsor)

Citi Research, part of Citigroup (NYSE: C), has identified Aave (CRYPTO: AAVE) as a potential leader in lending for tokenized assets once they move on-chain. The Citi Aave note highlights the importance of collateral mobility as one of the key benefits of tokenization. Collateral mobility allows users to pledge tokenized assets—like a blockchain version of Treasury funds—as loan security without the delays of traditional bank systems.

Aave operates as a lending protocol, enabling users to borrow cryptocurrencies by locking up their assets as collateral. Citi's interest positions Aave as one of the few decentralized finance (DeFi) applications a major bank has publicly named as possible plumbing for tokenized markets.

Thapana_Studio / Shutterstock.com

Despite this endorsement, AAVE continues to struggle. As of October 20, 2026, the token trades at $148, down 7.4% over the past week and 2.1% in the last 24 hours. Moreover, it is now down 77% from its May 2021 peak of $662.

While public summaries of Citi's report do not specify a price target for AAVE or name any banks or funds that have committed to using Aave, the question remains: Can Wall Street's support for Aave's framework help the token regain lost value?

Citi's Thesis Points Straight at Aave's Horizon Market
Anjelika Melnychenko / Shutterstock.com

Citi's analysis focuses on a service Aave has already built. On August 26, 2025, Aave Labs, the protocol's primary developer, launched Aave Horizon. This lending market operates on Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) and allows institutions and qualified users to borrow stablecoins—tokens tied to the U.S. dollar—against real-world assets.

In Horizon, real-world assets refer to tokenized funds containing U.S. Treasury bills and AAA-rated collateralized loan obligations—bundles of corporate loans categorized by risk. Initial collateral options were provided by Superstate and Centrifuge, with Horizon collaborating with Ripple and VanEck.

title: What Is Citigroup (C) Signaling With China Talks And Its AI Reset?
detail:
What Is Citigroup (C) Signaling With China Talks And Its AI Reset?
Bailey Pemberton
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:14 AM MST 3 min read
C
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup (NYSE:C) was the subject of formal talks between US and Chinese officials about its access to China's financial market.

US and Chinese representatives held these discussions as part of broader engagement on financial services, focusing on Citigroup's operating permissions in China.

Citigroup expanded and reshaped its central AI leadership group by hiring senior talent from Google and moving multiple executives into new roles.

The US China talks on Citigroup's market access and the reset of its AI leadership are only part of this bank's story. Check out 6 other big wins that Citigroup investors should know about.

This kind of AI build out is not unique to Citigroup. There is a wider set of stocks tied to the required infrastructure behind it 55 AI infrastructure stocks.

NYSE:C Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026

Citigroup is a US based banking group with a market value of about $205.7 billion. It provides lending, payments, trading and advisory services to consumers, corporates and governments, so moves on Chinese market access and central AI leadership touch both its global reach and core operating toolkit.

Does the team leading Citigroup have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.

Citigroup's China talks and AI hires test the "productivity plus reach" narrative

The Citigroup Narrative hangs on a simple idea. The bank is trying to turn a global services footprint, heavier digital payments use and AI driven efficiency into better long term returns while keeping regulatory risk in check, and this news cuts directly across all three levers.

"The main requirement is that Citigroup continues to convert its services growth, AI driven efficiency efforts and business simplification into sustained double digit returns on tangible common equity..."

See how the full story points towards a $151 fair value for Citigroup.

The Bangkok market access talks fit the story that services and cross border payments are the engine of Citigroup's future, because broader China permissions would feed exactly those flows. What complicates the picture is regulatory risk. The same policymakers being courted for access also police sanctions and controls that analysts already flag as a key vulnerability.

The AI leadership reshuffle, with senior hires from Google and a build out under David Griffiths, speaks directly to the productivity side of the thesis. At the same time, a centralised AI team, restricted agent access to accounts and a new responsible AI unit raise execution questions on whether compliance, infrastructure and cost can keep pace with the ambition. The unresolved piece is whether these AI and China pushes can lift returns faster than they raise complexity.
